editorial:
Imagine being stuck between your dad's dream of running a souvlaki shop and your own secret wish to shine in high school. You get to follow Soula, a girl who doesn't fit the usual cheerleader mold at all, as she navigates the high-pressure world of 1990s cheerleading. The vibe is super nostalgic and cozy, mixing funny family arguments with the stress of trying to fit in. It feels like a warm hug of a movie, focusing on the struggle to be yourself when everyone else expects you to be something different. You will definitely root for Soula as she tries to balance her Greek heritage with her new passion.

What really makes this work is the chemistry between the family members and the funny way the cheer scenes are handled. The pacing is brisk, though some of the drama feels a bit predictable. Still, the acting is genuine and keeps you invested. If you want a feel-good night, you should definitely stream this in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best colors, or maybe rent it on Apple TV if you are on the go. It is a great pick for a family movie night where you just want to smile and feel inspired.
endingExplained: In the final act, Soula leads her team through a massive competition. Despite her lack of experience, her unique spirit helps them nail their routine. Her father finally sees how happy she is and realizes that his daughter's happiness is more important than the family business. He cheers her on from the sidelines, showing he accepts her. The movie ends with Soula finding a perfect balance between her culture and her own dreams.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves underdog stories and family comedies.
